participants.note: ACKed the PR, noting pros and cons, while suggesting a while loop for over-capacity eviction
ACKed; argued retaining broadcast stats in RPC output is valuable for diagnostics and external clients
Noted a docstring nit regarding MarkReceived
tACKed, noted minor edge case regarding mempool invalidation before receiving TX message
Reviewed code structure, suggested ranges refactor, commit reordering, and release notes
Concept NACKed; argued keeping finished txs adds unnecessary memory and complexity for a niche use case and private broadcast should not expand into omni-broadcast logic

claims.harm: unbounded memory usage in the private broadcast queue could lead to out-of-memory crashes
claims.quote: With this PR, unless the caller is careful to abortprivatebroadcast, it seems you could get to an OOM situation
claims.settled_by_quote: Pops the earliest added no-longer-pending tx if there are 10k entries, due to the limit from #35406.

claims.harm: re-adding an existing transaction does not reset time_added, making it immediately stale if originally added more than 5 minutes ago
claims.quote: I think we should also set time_added to now() here, otherwise you're not resetting the entire state of the transaction.
claims.settled_by_quote: Reset time_added in Add(). Cover this in unit test.

claims.harm: getprivatebroadcastinfo RPC continues to report attempts_remaining after a transaction has already been received back
claims.quote: nit: attempts_remaining might need to report zero once it's reported received and not being retried later
claims.settled_by_quote: Set attempts_remaining to 0 when already received back.

claims.harm: adds complexity and memory retention for a narrow set of users, expanding private broadcast towards an omni-broadcast queue
claims.quote: concept NACK for now. I'm not persuaded this change is net positive. An average user simply will not need this feature

claims.harm: using if instead of while when evicting over-capacity transactions only removes one element, which may leave the queue over the limit
claims.quote: The if body removes at most one element, but the condition checks for larger. So there is no guarantee, that after the if m_transactions.size() < m_max_transactions.

support.reason: IMO it falls flat because the stats disappear once the transaction comes back and the best way to improve that is to not remove them from the RPC output like this PR does. The stats contain information like to whom we sent the transaction and at what time and when did we receive it back and from whom. This info can't be derived by looking at the mempool.

The extra complexity is encapsulated rather well into the private broadcast implementation. The received info can be useful for some clients. Received info can be especially useful in case of a future delayed broadcast feature. Overall, I'm for it.

result.notes: instagibbs's concept NACK remains open, objecting to keeping finished transactions in memory and expanding private broadcast into an omni-broadcast queue. optout21 also noted an open non-blocking edge case regarding the use of if rather than while in queue capacity eviction.
